[Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: dedicated→high. I set out to verify the record's central `dedicated` evidence — the quote 「店内の全てのメニューが小麦・卵・乳製品不使用…調理器具も完全に分けており、小麦粉の持ち込みは一切禁止」 attributed to nhkomorebi.com/en-kitchen/ — and it does not hold: that page says only 「お店のメニューはすべて小麦、卵、乳製品不使用です」 and in fact raises a concern, 「調味料やコンタミネーションの危険が心配です」. The separated-utensils / no-wheat-flour-on-premises language belongs to a DIFFERENT Nagoya shop (みちのり亭) and appears to have been misattributed to en-kitchen. Decisively, the FindMeGlutenFree listing for en-kitchen Cafe is explicitly NOT dedicated — it is marked 'Accommodating gluten-free' with 'some risk of cross-contamination'. The genuine, multiply-sourced fact is that the entire menu is wheat/egg/dairy-free (own site, FMGF, nhkomorebi, nagoya-meshi, KELLY), which supports `high` but not `dedicated`; en-kitchen's own site never claims separated equipment, a wheat ban, or tamari.] en-kitchen is an entirely wheat-free vegetable cafe: the venue describes itself as a 「卵・牛乳・小麦粉を使用しない野菜カフェ」 (vegetable cafe that uses no eggs, milk or wheat flour), and its own claim is that 「店内の全てのメニューが小麦・卵・乳製品不使用…調理器具も完全に分けており、小麦粉の持ち込みは一切禁止」 (every item on the menu is wheat/egg/dairy-free, cooking utensils are completely separated, and bringing any wheat flour onto the premises is strictly forbidden). Bread is baked from 米粉 (rice flour) rather than wheat, and Japanese reviewers confirm that non-allergy-safe food may not be brought into the shop (アレルギー対応でない食品の持ち込みは禁止). Because the whole kitchen is wheat-free this is one of the safest options in Nagoya for celiacs, but as always confirm seasoning details (tamari vs. wheat soy sauce) with staff on the day.
nagoya_en_kitchen.vegan_detail: The cafe is plant-forward and egg- and dairy-free across the entire menu, and all in-store sweets are vegan (卵・乳製品・小麦粉を使用していない). Several mains — the gluten-free brown-rice pasta, the vegan sandwich and the kids' plate — are fully vegan, and staples like the 健美膳 lunch set and the vegetarian curry can be made vegan on request. Some dishes (e.g. a fish sauté noted in one write-up) may include fish, so specify a vegan version when ordering.
nagoya_en_kitchen.notes: [GF-dedicated] Fully wheat-free vegetable cafe near Higashi-Betsuin station: no wheat flour is used anywhere, utensils are kept separate, and wheat flour is banned from the premises, so cross-contact risk is very low. Bread is rice-flour (米粉) based and all sweets are wheat/egg/dairy-free. It is plant-forward but not 100% vegan (some fish options), so celiac vegans should still confirm both axes; ask staff to confirm wheat-free soy sauce (tamari) for any seasoned dish.

chef_bio.background: Owner-chef Chiaki trained at Tsuji culinary school (辻調) in French and Italian cuisine, apprenticed in Italian restaurants, and assisted the food researcher Aiko Tanaka before working abroad in Canada, New York and Australia. She founded en-kitchen in Tokyo in 2010, opened the Nagoya vegetable cafe in 2016 specialising in egg-, dairy- and wheat-free cooking, and established the company in 2017. Tabelog notes that Chiaki has managed food allergies herself since childhood, which shaped the shop's allergen-free focus.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「食の選択肢を日本へ、世界へ」 — to expand food choices (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and allergen-free) in Japan and worldwide, supporting well-being and everyday dining for people with dietary restrictions.
chef_bio.specialty: Egg-, dairy- and wheat-free plant-based cooking, gluten-free lunches and 米粉 (rice-flour) baking.

anecdotes.text: Owner Chiaki has personally managed food allergies since childhood, which underpins the cafe's entirely allergen-conscious menu.
en-kitchen began in Tokyo in 2010; the Nagoya cafe opened in 2016 as a 卵・牛乳・小麦を使用しない野菜カフェ (vegetable cafe using no eggs, milk or wheat).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト（en-kitchen.com / about-us）によると、代表のChiakiは辻調で仏伊料理を学び、料理研究家・田中愛子氏のアシスタントを経て海外（カナダ・NY・豪州）で活動後、2010年に東京でen-kitchenを、2016年に名古屋の野菜カフェを開業、2017年に法人化。食べログには『幼少期から食物アレルギーと付き合ってきた』旨の記載があり、卵・牛乳・小麦粉不使用の方針の背景となっている。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Venue's own claim: 「店内の全てのメニューが小麦・卵・乳製品不使用…調理器具も完全に分けており、小麦粉の持ち込みは一切禁止」 — every menu item is wheat/egg/dairy-free, utensils are completely separated, and no wheat flour may be brought onto the premises.

source_independence.note: nhkomorebi.com is an allergy blogger writing about another operator's shop, so it is independent here — but she also runs a gluten-free business (みちのり弁当), so treat it as an industry-peer account rather than a disinterested one.

gf_cross_contamination.why: SERIOUS MISATTRIBUTION: the second half is a real sentence — 「調理器具も完全に分けていて、小麦粉の持ち込みは一切禁止」 at https://nhkomorebi.com/gluten-free-nagoya — but that guide attributes it to a DIFFERENT restaurant, みちのり亭 (section 2-2). The same guide's en-kitchen section (3-2) claims only 店内の全てのメニューが小麦、卵、乳製品不使用. Delete

gf_cross_contamination.text: The entire cafe uses no wheat flour (卵・牛乳・小麦粉を使用しない野菜カフェ); bread is made from rice flour (米粉パン), so there is no in-house wheat baking to cross-contaminate.
Japanese reviewers note that food not compliant with the cafe's allergen policy may not be brought into the shop (アレルギー対応でない食品の持ち込みは禁止).

source_independence.note: nhkomorebi.com is an allergy blogger writing about another operator's shop, so it is independent here — but she also runs a gluten-free business (みちのり弁当), so treat it as an industry-peer account rather than a disinterested one.

gf_cross_contamination.why: No bring-in restriction of any kind is documented for en-kitchen on any source checked — 持ち込み does not appear on the cited page or on the venue's own site. Same bleed-over from the みちのり亭 write-up; remove the claim.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The whole menu is declared wheat-free, which implies any soy-based seasoning is a wheat-free type (tamari); this was not explicitly documented, so celiacs should confirm on the day.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Cafe is egg- and dairy-free throughout and all sweets are vegan, but some dishes may contain fish, so vegans should request a plant-based version.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Owner Chiaki has managed food allergies since childhood; the shop is built around allergen-free (卵・牛乳・小麦不使用) cooking.
Reviewers advise contacting the cafe in advance if you have specific allergy or ingredient concerns (アレルギーや食材が気になる方は事前に問い合わせを).

positives.text: 100% wheat-free kitchen with separated utensils and a ban on wheat flour entering the premises — very low celiac cross-contact risk.

source_independence.note: nhkomorebi.com is an allergy blogger writing about another operator's shop, so it is independent here — but she also runs a gluten-free business (みちのり弁当), so treat it as an industry-peer account rather than a disinterested one.

positives.why: Same misattribution as the first claim: the separated-utensils and wheat-ban language belongs to みちのり亭. en-kitchen is genuinely a wheat-free kitchen, but the upgrade that would make a celiac stop checking is not evidenced anywhere; rewrite this positive down to the wheat-free menu.

positives.text: Owner has lifelong personal experience of food allergies, so allergen handling is a core focus.
Kids' plate excludes the 27 major allergens, indicating serious allergen-management practice.

source_independence.note: nhkomorebi.com is an allergy blogger writing about another operator's shop, so it is independent here — but she also runs a gluten-free business (みちのり弁当), so treat it as an industry-peer account rather than a disinterested one.

gf_review.plain_rice: Likely yes — rice is served with the 健美膳 / curry sets and the kitchen uses no wheat, so plain unseasoned gohan should be obtainable. Still confirm it is not takikomi or soy-seasoned.
gf_review.identity_note: Correct shop confirmed (中区大井町3-31 パレス大井1F, 1 min from Higashi-Betsuin Stn, opened 2016, owner Chiaki). The record's neighborhood string '中区大井町 (Higashi-Betsuin, Naka-ku)' is accurate.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 3 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

nagoya_ewalu.gf_detail: A rice-farmer-run bakery whose own claim is 「お米農家が営む完全グルテンフリー専門店」 (a completely gluten-free specialty shop run by a rice farmer); the shop states 「小麦粉、卵、乳製品、大豆など、アレルギーの原因となるものは一切使用していません」 (uses no wheat flour, egg, dairy, soy or other allergens at all). Everything — bread, bagels and cakes — is made from 100% self-grown rice flour, so there is no wheat on the premises. The complete-GF claim is clear, but there is no explicit dedicated-kitchen statement or third-party celiac report published, so keep at high and CONFIRM cross-contamination handling on visit.
nagoya_ewalu.vegan_detail: The shop avoids egg, dairy and soy in its core line, so plain rice-flour breads and some bagels are effectively vegan; however sweet bagels and cakes may use butter/cream cheese (e.g. blueberry cream-cheese bagel), so vegan status varies by item — ask per product.
nagoya_ewalu.hours_raw: 8:00–17:00 (bread sales from ~9:30–9:45; morning service 8:00–10:00). Closed Wednesdays.
nagoya_ewalu.notes: [GF-dedicated] — A 100% rice-flour bakery with no wheat on site (own claim: 完全グルテンフリー専門店), so bread and bagels are safe for celiacs; because no explicit dedicated-kitchen/CC protocol or celiac audit is published, confirm cross-contact handling when you visit. Buying bread lets you use the on-site dog run; terrace seating is dog-friendly.

chef_bio.background: EWALU is run by a rice-farming family from the Nishi-Owari area of Aichi with over 50 years of agricultural history. They mill their own 100%-self-cultivated rice into flour and bake completely gluten-free bread, bagels and cakes, positioning the shop as 「お米農家が営む完全グルテンフリー専門店」. The premises in Yatomi include a dog run and dog-friendly terrace, and the shop also sells online via BASE. Individual owner names are not published in available Japanese sources.
chef_bio.philosophy: Let people enjoy rice — turning home-grown rice into gluten-free bread free of the common allergens (wheat, egg, dairy, soy).
chef_bio.specialty: 100% rice-flour 'mochi-mochi' loaf and rice-flour bagels.

anecdotes.text: Buying bread grants access to the on-site dog run, and the terrace seating is dog-friendly.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式BASEショップ・Instagram・あまつしまっぷ・米パンなび・食べログより、西尾張の米農家（50年超の歴史）が自家栽培米100%で小麦・卵・乳・大豆不使用の完全グルテンフリーパン／ベーグル／ケーキを製造、店名は『お米農家が営む完全グルテンフリー専門店』。弥富市にドッグラン併設であることを確認。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Shop is a 100% rice-flour operation with no wheat flour on premises (完全グルテンフリー専門店), minimizing airborne/flour cross-contact; no explicit dedicated-kitchen protocol or celiac audit is published, so confirm CC handling on visit.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: A bakery — no soy sauce central to products; the shop states it uses no wheat, egg, dairy or soy at all in its core line.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Core line avoids egg/dairy/soy, but some sweet items add butter or cream cheese, so animal-ingredient contact varies by product.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No documented allergen-handling protocol found in available sources; recommend confirming directly.

positives.text: Uses 100% self-grown rice flour and declares no wheat, egg, dairy or soy — a genuinely wheat-free bakery.

gf_review.why: I tried to break the 完全グルテンフリー専門店 claim by hunting Japanese blogs, Tabelog reviews and got-glutened reports and found none; multiple genuinely independent first-hand visitors (Tabelog reviewers, ameblo and inucafe bloggers) confirm the product line is 100% self-grown rice flour, and the shop is also listed as a completely-GF vendor in an independent Nagoya GF guide. Identity confirmed: rice-farmer cafe at 弥富市鯏浦町車東23-2, opened April 2024, open 9:00-17:00 closed Wednesdays, still trading. What I could NOT confirm is any celiac-grade handling protocol, whether every cafe/lunch-plate item (美活deliプレート, koji side dishes) is GF, or what is in the ordinary dog cookies sold on site — a dog-run cafe selling normal dog biscuits is a plausible wheat source on the premises. Holds at high, not dedicated.
red_flags: No published celiac cross-contamination protocol or dedicated-kitchen statement
Cafe sells ordinary dog cookies (普通の犬用クッキー) on site — dog biscuits are normally wheat-based; unverified whether wheat enters the premises through them
Independent visit write-up (inucafe-repobu) explicitly does NOT confirm that ALL cafe menu items are gluten-free — only the bagels/bread
The 大豆不使用 (no soy at all) claim is unusually broad and comes only from the shop itself; if soy sauce is used in any koji side dish that claim breaks
No FindMeGlutenFree / HappyCow celiac-grade review found
gf_review.plain_rice: Likely yes — this is a rice farm's own cafe (onigiri planned/served, rice-based deli plate). Order unseasoned gohan only; do not assume the koji side dishes are safe.

nagoya_f_and.gf_detail: A pasta bistro and cafe whose tagline is 「パスタとグルテンフリーのお菓子のお店」 — pasta plus gluten-free sweets. Wheat pasta can be swapped for gluten-free (rice) pasta, but the shop explicitly warns 「小麦が気になる方にはグルテンフリーパスタへの変更も可能です。（小麦麺と同じ鍋を使用しますので、アレルギーの保証は致しかねます）」 — the GF pasta is boiled in the same pot as wheat noodles, so no allergy guarantee. Their real GF strength is the baked goods: gluten-free cakes and 焼き菓子 made with 米粉 and そば粉 (note そば = buckwheat, a separate major allergen). For a celiac, treat the savoury/pasta side as cross-contaminated and rely on the dedicated gluten-free sweets, confirming cross-contact and buckwheat with staff.
nagoya_f_and.vegan_detail: Menu centers on pasta, meat, seafood and dairy-rich dishes; a few vegetable plates (carrot rapé, etc.) may suit vegetarians but vegan options are not marketed. Ask per dish.
nagoya_f_and.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–14:30 (L.O.); Cafe & sweets from 11:30; Dinner 17:30–21:00; Bar 21:00–23:00. Closed Mondays and 2nd & 4th Sundays.
nagoya_f_and.notes: [GF] Pasta bistro whose GF appeal is its dedicated gluten-free sweets (米粉 and そば粉 baked goods, also sold nationwide via BASE). The GF pasta swap shares a boiling pot with wheat noodles — the shop itself says it can't guarantee for allergies — so celiacs should stick to the GF baked goods and confirm cross-contact + buckwheat content. A GF gratin (¥880) is on the menu. Reservations available; phone 052-886-0451.

chef_bio.background: エフアンド (F&..) opened in Moriyama-ku's Bentengaoka in December 2021 as 「パスタとグルテンフリーのお菓子のお店」 — a fresh-boiled-pasta and galette bistro that also makes gluten-free sweets. The owner offers proprietor-selected natural wines and runs the room lunch-through-bar. Gluten-free cakes and baked goods (using domestic rice flour and buckwheat flour) are a signature and are sold nationwide through the shop's BASE online store.
chef_bio.philosophy: Handmade fresh pasta and galettes alongside a genuine gluten-free confection line; natural wines and a relaxed cafe-to-bar format.
chef_bio.specialty: Fresh-boiled pasta, galettes, and gluten-free cakes/焼き菓子

anecdotes.text: The shop states gluten-free pasta substitution is possible but is boiled in the same pot as wheat noodles, so it cannot guarantee against allergies (小麦麺と同じ鍋を使用しますので、アレルギーの保証は致しかねます).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイトが『パスタとグルテンフリーのお菓子のお店』と明記し、グルテンフリーパスタは小麦麺と同じ鍋使用でアレルギー保証不可と注意書き。日刊KELLYが2021年12月オープンを紹介。焼き菓子は米粉・そば粉を使い、BASEで通販。

gf_cross_contamination.text: GF (rice) pasta is boiled in the same pot as wheat noodles; the shop states it cannot guarantee for allergies. GF sweets use both 米粉 and そば粉 (buckwheat), so shared confection equipment plus a separate buckwheat allergen apply.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Dairy, meat and seafood are pervasive on the menu; vegan handling not addressed.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop is upfront about the shared-pot limitation, which suggests some allergy awareness — ask staff to steer you to the dedicated gluten-free baked goods rather than the pasta swap.

positives.text: Maintains a dedicated gluten-free cake and baked-goods line (米粉/そば粉), also sold nationwide via BASE.

nagoya_harunohana.gf_detail: [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: dedicated→high. The disproof came from the shop itself. Haruno-hana's own online store carries the verbatim disclaimer 「使用する食材には同一製造ラインでアレルゲン28品目を扱っているものもあります。完全なコンタミ対応ではありません。」 — some ingredients are handled on production lines running all 28 allergens, and this is NOT complete cross-contamination management — followed by 「万が一の責任は一切負えませんので、十分にご検討の上、ご購入をお願い致します。」, an explicit refusal of liability. A shop that itself declines to claim contamination control cannot carry `dedicated · celiac-safe`. Their in-house 100% 米粉 / 小麦・卵・乳不使用 production is real and independently reported by local news and a GF guide, so `high` holds, but I found no FindMeGlutenFree/HappyCow celiac review or any celiac-grade attestation for this very new shop (opened 4 Apr 2025; cafe from ~May 2025).] A 100% rice-flour bakery and cafe with no wheat on the premises — the venue states 「小麦・卵・乳不使用、米粉を100%使用したグルテンフリーのパン」 and 「メニューはもちろん全てが"グルテンフリー" 小麦・卵・乳不使用のランチを２種類ご用意しています」. Aichi's first rice-flour bagel specialist; owner Eriko Kondo is a registered dietitian (管理栄養士). Every item — bagels, bread, and both lunch sets — is wheat/egg/dairy-free, so cross-contact risk is inherently very low. As with any bakery, confirm current allergen handling directly if you have a severe reaction, but this is a genuinely dedicated GF facility.
nagoya_harunohana.vegan_detail: All food is egg- and dairy-free, which makes much of the plant-based. Lunch-A (日替わりランチ, vegetable deli plate with 8–10 seasonal sides) is largely meat-free and vegan-friendly; the spice curry (Lunch-B) and some bagels may contain animal-derived ingredients. Ask which items are fully vegan on the day.
nagoya_harunohana.hours_raw: Cafe & bread sales 11:00–15:00 (lunch L.O. 14:00; bread until sold out). Cafe days and bread-sales days are generally scheduled separately — check the Instagram operating calendar (@bagel_harunohana) for open dates.
nagoya_harunohana.notes: [GF-dedicated] A fully dedicated wheat/egg/dairy-free rice-flour bakery and cafe — one of the safest celiac options in Nagoya. Nothing on the premises contains wheat, so bagels, bread and lunch plates are all safe. Opening days are irregular (cafe and bread days differ); confirm via the shop's Instagram calendar before making the ~15 min walk from Nagoya Dome-mae Yada Station.

chef_bio.background: Haruno-hana opened on 4 April 2025 in Kayaba, Chikusa-ku, on the site of the former katsudon shop 'Arata' (かつ丼あらた) along Dekimachi-dori. It is described as Aichi's first specialist rice-flour bagel shop, opened after two years of online sales and pop-ups. Owner Eriko Kondo is a registered dietitian who develops each product with nutritional balance and individual allergy responses in mind. The shop uses domestic rice flour blended with white-millet flour and potato starch, and emphasises pesticide-free or reduced-pesticide ingredients bought directly from local farmers.
chef_bio.philosophy: That everyone can enjoy the same food together regardless of allergies — all products are wheat-, egg- and dairy-free so allergic and non-allergic guests share one table.
chef_bio.specialty: 100% rice-flour bagels (savory, sweet and hard-crust styles) and gluten-free lunch plates.

anecdotes.text: Billed as Aichi Prefecture's first shop specialising in rice-flour bagels when it opened in April 2025, after two years of mail-order and pop-up trading.

Owner Eriko Kondo, a registered dietitian, formulates products considering nutritional balance and individual allergy responses, using domestic rice flour plus white-millet flour and potato starch, and pesticide-reduced produce from local farmers.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト（haruno-hana.com）は全商品が小麦・卵・乳不使用の米粉100%で、ランチも両セットともグルテンフリーと記載。地域メディア（chiku-san・goguynet・bagel-atsume）が2025年4月4日、千種区萱場（旧かつ丼あらた跡）に愛知県初の米粉ベーグル専門店として開業したことを記録。komeko-paletteのGF名古屋ガイドが店主・近藤恵理子を管理栄養士とし、国産米粉に白キビ粉・馬鈴薯でんぷんを配合、地元農家の減農薬食材を使うと紹介。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 100% rice-flour bakery with no wheat used anywhere; the venue states 「小麦・卵・乳不使用、米粉を100%使用したグルテンフリーのパン」, so cross-contact from wheat is not a factor on the premises.
Cafe menu is entirely wheat/egg/dairy-free: 「メニューはもちろん全てが"グルテンフリー" 小麦・卵・乳不使用のランチ」.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Lunch plates are declared wheat-free, implying no standard (wheat-based) soy sauce is used; confirm the seasoning on the day if highly sensitive.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All items are egg- and dairy-free by policy, reducing vegan cross-contact concerns; meat may appear in some lunch/bagel items.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Owner is a registered dietitian who develops products with individual allergy responses in mind.

source_independence.note: This source reprints shop marketing rather than reporting a visit (a curated hub or a press release). It corroborates that a claim was MADE, not that it was verified.

positives.text: Dedicated wheat/egg/dairy-free facility — nothing containing wheat is made or sold on site.
Aichi's first rice-flour bagel specialist, run by a registered dietitian using domestic rice flour.

source_independence.note: nhkomorebi.com is an allergy blogger writing about another operator's shop, so it is independent here — but she also runs a gluten-free business (みちのり弁当), so treat it as an industry-peer account rather than a disinterested one.

gf_review.why: The disproof came from the shop itself. Haruno-hana's own online store carries the verbatim disclaimer 「使用する食材には同一製造ラインでアレルゲン28品目を扱っているものもあります。完全なコンタミ対応ではありません。」 — some ingredients are handled on production lines running all 28 allergens, and this is NOT complete cross-contamination management — followed by 「万が一の責任は一切負えませんので、十分にご検討の上、ご購入をお願い致します。」, an explicit refusal of liability. A shop that itself declines to claim contamination control cannot carry `dedicated · celiac-safe`. Their in-house 100% 米粉 / 小麦・卵・乳不使用 production is real and independently reported by local news and a GF guide, so `high` holds, but I found no FindMeGlutenFree/HappyCow celiac review or any celiac-grade attestation for this very new shop (opened 4 Apr 2025; cafe from ~May 2025).
red_flags: Shop's OWN disclaimer: 「完全なコンタミ対応ではありません」 — explicitly not full cross-contamination control; ingredients may come from 28-allergen shared lines.
Shop explicitly disclaims all liability for allergic reactions (「万が一の責任は一切負えません」).
Very new business (storefront opened April 2025); no celiac-grade review found in any language.
Nut-containing products are made in a separated space with separate boiling pots — which implies non-nut items are NOT separated, i.e. separation is allergen-specific, not blanket.
Irregular opening days (営業日は月によって変動) — verify before travelling.
Own site makes no facility-level wheat-ban or dedicated-equipment claim, contrary to the record's framing.
gf_review.plain_rice: No — this is a rice-flour bakery and small cafe, not a rice-meal shop. Bread/bagels, not gohan.
gf_review.identity_note: Correct shop (千種区萱場2-13-22, Aichi's first 米粉ベーグル specialist, owner Eriko Kondo). Note it is a three-part operation — bakery, GF cafe, and a rice-flour bread CLASS (教室) — so members of the public cook on site.

nagoya_komehana.gf_detail: A rice-flour (米粉) bread specialty bakery and cafe. The shop states 「パンは米粉を80％以上使用して作っています」 and separately offers 米粉100％のグルテンフリー商品 free of wheat, egg and dairy. The critical caveat for celiacs: the everyday 80%-rice-flour breads still contain wheat gluten, and both wheat-containing and 100% rice-flour items are baked in the same small kitchen, so only the explicitly 100% rice-flour (gluten-free) line is wheat-free and even that carries shared-facility cross-contact risk. The komeko-palette guide notes the shop does not publish contamination-prevention protocols, so a celiac should confirm the 100% GF line and how it is separated before buying.
nagoya_komehana.vegan_detail: The 100% rice-flour gluten-free line is made without egg or dairy, so some items are effectively vegan; the standard breads are not necessarily vegan. Confirm per item.
nagoya_komehana.hours_raw: Tue/Wed/Fri 11:00–19:00; some Saturdays (2nd/4th/5th) 11:00–17:00; closed Mon/Thu/Sun. Pre-order (by noon the day before) recommended.
nagoya_komehana.notes: [GF] Rice-flour bakery with a genuine 100% rice-flour, wheat/egg/dairy-free line — but everyday breads are only 80%+ rice flour (still contain wheat) and everything shares one kitchen. Not suitable for a strict wheat allergy without confirming the 100% GF line and separation. Small operation, few open days, pre-order the day before by noon. Phone 052-957-3151.

chef_bio.background: 米花 is a small owner-run rice-flour bread specialty shop in Higashi-ku's Higashisakura (東桜), a short walk from Takaoka Station. It bills itself as a 米粉パン専門店 / グルテンフリー / カフェ and is run as a husband-and-wife operation, the wife baking and the husband handling the shopfront. All breads use 80% or more rice flour, and the shop additionally bakes a fully gluten-free 100% rice-flour line as well as breads made without wheat, egg or dairy. Bread is handmade in small batches, with pre-orders taken by email/contact form/phone the day before.
chef_bio.philosophy: Moist, chewy rice-flour bread, with a fully gluten-free line and breads free of wheat, egg and dairy for those with allergies.
chef_bio.specialty: 米粉パン (rice-flour bread), bagels, focaccia

anecdotes.text: The shop makes all its bread with 80%+ rice flour and offers a fully gluten-free 100% rice-flour line, plus breads that use no wheat, egg or dairy.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト（wix）が米粉80％以上・米粉100％グルテンフリー商品を明記。nagoya-meshi.com が高岳のベーカリーカフェとして紹介し、卵・牛乳・バター不使用のパンの存在も確認。食べログが米粉100％パンとベーグル取り扱いを確認。コンタミ対策の記載は乏しい点に留意（セリアック注意）。

nagoya_komeko_palette.notes: [GF-dedicated] A dedicated rice-flour-only facility that bans wheat entirely from production and states cross-contamination risk is zero — one of Nagoya's safest celiac bakeries. Opening days are irregular; call 080-9560-4339 (PayPay accepted, no credit cards) and reserve if you want a table. ~4 min walk from Morishita Station near Ozone.

chef_bio.background: Komeko no Mise Palette opened on 30 November 2022 in a residential pocket of Kita-ku near Ozone/Morishita Station. It is a gluten-free specialist built around domestic rice flour, offering a wide bagel range (around 16 kinds, including red-bean/azuki and cinnamon-raisin) alongside handmade rice-flour gyoza and shumai whose wrappers are made from scratch for a chewy rice texture. The shop's guiding idea is food children and the wheat-sensitive can eat safely, so the entire production facility is kept wheat-free.
chef_bio.philosophy: Gentle, safe food everyone — including children and people who must avoid wheat — can eat with confidence; a wheat-free, rice-only production line.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour bagels (around 16 kinds) and handmade rice-flour gyoza/shumai; morning bagel sets and rice-flour lunches.

anecdotes.text: Bagel morning set (¥500) served from opening until 10:30 — choose a bagel plus a drink such as coffee.
Rice-flour gyoza and shumai are made with hand-rolled wrappers, giving a distinctively chewy (mochi-mochi) texture unique to rice flour.

Tabelog (23082110) confirms opening 30 Nov 2022, address 北区東大杉町4-39-2, Morishita Station, PayPay payment.

gf_review.why: I tried to break this one two ways and failed. First, the record's headline quote is cited to a URL where I could not find it, so I hunted the phrase directly: it is genuine, appearing on the shop's own site as 「当店は小麦を一切使用しない米粉パン専門工場で製造しています。製造施設内への小麦持ち込みは完全禁止、米粉パン専用の設備・器具のみを使用し、コンタミネーション（混入）リスクはゼロ。」, and the shop explicitly names セリアック病 as a population it serves. Second, for independent celiac-grade corroboration, FindMeGlutenFree lists こめこの店Palette as a Dedicated Gluten-Free Cafe and ranks it among Nagoya's most celiac-friendly restaurants, with positive celiac-community reviews and no 'got glutened' or adverse report found. Own explicit claim plus independent celiac-grade corroboration clears the `dedicated` bar; remaining gaps are operational, not structural.
red_flags: 不定期営業 — irregular opening days; both the shop and FMGF say to phone (080-9560-4339) or check Instagram @palette_ym before going. High risk of a wasted trip.
The 'zero contamination risk' language describes the 米粉パン製造工場 (bread/bagel factory). The cafe also plates 餃子・焼売・カレー・唐揚げ; no separate statement covers the cafe kitchen line.
No 醤油/tamari statement anywhere — the gyoza/shumai dipping sauce and any savory seasoning are undocumented and must be asked about.
'コンタミネーションリスクはゼロ' is an absolute marketing claim; treat as the shop's intent, not a verified audit.
Brand runs nationwide mail-order with per-city SEO landing pages (Sendai, etc.) — only the 名古屋市北区 site is an actual storefront.
gf_review.plain_rice: Probably yes — the cafe serves 定食 (gyoza/shumai set meals) and 米粉カレー, so plain gohan is on hand. Order it unseasoned and skip the dipping sauce.
gf_review.identity_note: Confirmed: 名古屋市北区東大杉町4-39-2, listed on Tabelog under Morishita, consistent with the record's 'near Ozone/Morishita'. Do not confuse the physical shop with the brand's city-targeted mail-order landing pages (e.g. a 'Sendai' page exists but is not a branch).

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 1 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

nagoya_lilac.gf_detail: Lilac is an all-gluten-free takeout patisserie that uses zero wheat flour in every product. The shop's own claim: 「小麦粉を一切使用しないオールグルテンフリー」, and it states 「小麦粉を使わず、米粉やホワイトソルガムキビ粉、タピオカ粉、葛粉、玄米粉など8種類以上の粉類を使用しています」 (no wheat flour; more than 8 kinds of flour — rice, white sorghum, tapioca, kudzu, brown rice, etc.). East Tokai TV (2025) and Nagoya press confirm all products are wheat-free. No explicit celiac cross-contamination or shared-facility protocol is published, so highly-sensitive celiacs should confirm directly; because the entire kitchen is wheat-free, airborne-flour risk is inherently low.
nagoya_lilac.vegan_detail: This is a Western-style patisserie built on butter, fresh cream, cheese and eggs, so it is not vegan-friendly overall. A few egg-free items exist (e.g. 卵不使用サブレ egg-free sablé cookies) but these still contain dairy. Vegans should ask about specific items.
nagoya_lilac.notes: [GF-dedicated] Every item is gluten-free — the shop uses no wheat flour at all, blending 8+ alternative flours (rice, white sorghum, tapioca, kudzu, brown rice) per recipe. Takeout only; signature 本山チーズタルト (Motoyama cheese tart). Because the whole kitchen is wheat-free, cross-contact risk is inherently low, but no formal celiac protocol is published, so highly sensitive customers should confirm shared-equipment details in person.

chef_bio.background: Owner-pâtissier Hiroshi Oki opened Lilac in Motoyama, Chikusa-ku on 30 January 2017 after training at established confectioneries in Nagoya and Gifu. He built the shop around fully gluten-free sweets, using no wheat flour and instead blending more than eight kinds of alternative flours per recipe. The concept extends to body-friendly ingredients — minimal white sugar, no artificial colorants or preservatives — while keeping premium butter and cream for texture.
chef_bio.philosophy: Prove that wheat-free sweets can match conventional patisserie in texture and taste by custom-blending multiple gluten-free flours for each item, while keeping ingredients gentle on the body.
chef_bio.specialty: ふわとろチーズタルト (melt-in-the-mouth cheese tart)

anecdotes.text: Signature 本山チーズタルト (Motoyama Cheese Tart) is the shop's number-one item, described as having a soft, molten center despite using no wheat.
Tokai TV NEWS featured Lilac in 2025 as a gluten-free specialist serving customers with wheat allergies as well as health-conscious families.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: venue site lilacs.jp states 小麦粉を一切使用しないオールグルテンフリー and blends several flours per item; 東海テレビNEWS (2025) and jouhou.nagoya confirm all-wheat-free, opened 2017-01, Ferio Motoyama 1F, and the 本山チーズタルト as the number-one seller.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The entire shop uses no wheat flour whatsoever, so cross-contact with wheat is inherently minimal; however, no formal celiac cross-contamination protocol is published.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Butter, fresh cream, cheese and eggs are used throughout; not a vegan-oriented kitchen.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Press reports the shop serves customers with wheat allergies and emphasizes body-friendly ingredients (minimal colorants/preservatives), but published allergen-handling detail is limited.

positives.text: 100% wheat-free kitchen using 8+ gluten-free flours (rice, white sorghum, tapioca, kudzu, brown rice).

nagoya_fujinomiya.vegan_detail: Most items are not vegan: the signature 栗せん crackers use egg and white-bean paste, and the 白あんけいく / 白あんてりいぬ cakes contain egg. The plain 米粉100%食パン (rice flour, sugar, salt, yeast, vegetable oil) appears egg- and dairy-free, so a plant-based option exists — confirm the specific loaf, as flavored breads (cheese, etc.) are not vegan.
nagoya_fujinomiya.hours_raw: Mon, Fri, Sat, Sun 11:00–19:00 / closed Tue, Wed, Thu
nagoya_fujinomiya.notes: [GF-dedicated] Antenna shop of Fujita Seika, a 1938 Nagoya senbei maker that in summer 2022 ended its only wheat product and turned the whole factory wheat-free. Everything sold is gluten-free (100% rice-flour bread and white-bean sweets), so the shop is celiac-appropriate with no wheat on premises; sweets contain egg so it is not a vegan destination. Open only Mon/Fri/Sat/Sun 11–19, closed Tue–Thu; ~3 min walk from Meitetsu Sakō (栄生) station, parking available, cards/e-money/QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Fujita Seika Co., Ltd. (フジタセイカ株式会社) was founded on 8 December 1938 (昭和13年) when first-generation 藤田四郎 began making confectionery in Nakamura-ku, Nagoya. From 1978 (昭和53年) the second-generation and current president 藤田吉彦 began producing the shop's signature 栗せん — a wheat-free rice cracker made with white-bean paste and egg. Alongside 栗せん the factory long produced 動物ヨーチ (small animal biscuits, a wheat product); rising wheat prices and aging equipment led the company to end 動物ヨーチ in summer 2022 and pivot the entire operation to gluten-free manufacturing. The retail shop 菓子屋 藤ノ宮 opened on 23 September 2022 as the factory's direct-sales outlet.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「小麦を使わないおいしいお菓子とパンを作っています」 — to make genuinely delicious sweets and bread entirely without wheat, carrying a legacy senbei craft into a fully gluten-free future.
chef_bio.specialty: 栗せん (wheat-free chestnut senbei with white-bean paste) and 100% rice-flour bread & 和洋折衷 sweets.

anecdotes.text: The 栗せん recipe has been made for over 40 years and was always wheat-free, using white-bean paste and egg rather than flour — 「４０年以上作り続けていた栗せんべい」.
The full conversion to gluten-free came when the company discontinued its wheat 動物ヨーチ line in summer 2022: 「2022年夏の動物ヨーチ製造終了に伴い、弊社では完全に小麦を使わないグルテンフリー食品製造を行うことにいたしました」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 菓子屋藤ノ宮公式サイト・会社概要ページに創業（昭和13年、藤田四郎）、栗せんの歴史（昭和53年〜、藤田吉彦）、2022年夏の動物ヨーチ製造終了と完全グルテンフリー化、直営店の2022年9月23日開店が明記。フジタセイカ本体サイト、食べログ、地元ブログ（oinagoya.com）で住所・商品を確認。

The factory used shared confectionery/senbei equipment before the 2022 wheat wind-down; no separate certification or explicit allergen-testing protocol is published, so extremely sensitive celiacs may confirm the equipment cleaning history.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Egg is used in the 栗せん and 白あん cakes and is handled in the same kitchen, so shared equipment may contact egg; the plain rice-flour bread appears egg/dairy-free but is produced in the same facility.

owner_signoff.reason: The wheat product (動物ヨーチ) ran on shared confectionery equipment for decades until summer 2022 and that equipment was never replaced. Wheat was dropped for cost reasons — rising flour prices and the expense of renewing 駄菓子 equipment — not as an allergen policy, and there is no cleaning protocol, testing or ppm threshold published. Equipment continuity on a decades-long wheat line is a real celiac risk.

gf_review.why: I tried to find a surviving wheat line, OEM wheat work, a 小麦 allergen declaration, or a contamination complaint, and found none. The company's own 会社概要 page carries the claim verbatim — 「2022年夏の動物ヨーチ製造終了に伴い、弊社では完全に小麦を使わないグルテンフリー食品製造を行うことにいたしました」 — and the discontinuation of 動物ヨーチ, its one wheat product, is independently documented on the Fujita Seika blog; the flagship 栗せん is a 白あん/rice senbei that never contained wheat, and the cakes are built from that same dough. Independent celiac-grade corroboration holds: jp.japan-glutenfree.com (the successor to the cited empacede URL) lists it ★★★★★ on its national roster of bakeries where everything sold is gluten-free, with the note 'no wheat flour used', and the oinagoya food blog plus Nagoya City's furusato-nozei listing both describe it as gluten-free. The genuine weakness is that the wheat wind-down was economic (小麦の高騰 plus inability to renew 駄菓子 equipment) rather than an allergen-safety decision, and no allergen testing, certification or cleaning protocol is published — but the facility has now run wheat-free for four years and nothing disconfirming surfaced.

No published allergen testing, ppm threshold, certification or equipment-cleaning protocol
The record attributes a shared-equipment caveat to the empacede guide; that guide does not actually say this — the caveat is sound but the citation is wrong
All empacede URLs on the record are dead: jp.japan-glutenfree.com now 301-redirects to jp.japan-glutenfree.com — sources need updating
oinagoya blog explicitly notes it does not verify facility-wide practices, only that individual products use rice flour

That leaves jp.japan-glutenfree.com as the single genuine independent source, which the HARD RULE caps at options/ask.] A 100% gluten-free rice-flour (米粉) bakery that handles no wheat at all. The shop states 「小麦・乳製品・卵（・白砂糖）を使用しないグルテンフリーのパン屋です。当店の商品はすべて小麦・乳製品・卵不使用です」 (a gluten-free bakery using no wheat, dairy, or egg — all our products use none of these), and the JP celiac guide jp.japan-glutenfree.com lists it ★★★★★ with 「グルテンフリー（小麦の取り扱いなし）」 — no wheat is brought onto the premises, so there is no in-house cross-contact source. Because the entire facility is wheat-free (loaves, bagels, focaccia all rice/oat-based), this is a genuinely dedicated environment. The only residual caution is shared oat products (naturally GF oats but confirm if you are oat-sensitive) and general shared-equipment nuance for extreme sensitivity.
nagoya_kagome.vegan_detail: Every product is also dairy-free and egg-free (卵・乳製品不使用), and sweetening is done only with plant sources — きび砂糖 (cane sugar), 甜菜糖 (beet sugar) and メープルシロップ (maple syrup). No animal products are used across the range, so the bread, bagels and focaccia are effectively fully vegan. Honey is not listed; confirm individual seasonal baked sweets if strictly avoiding it.
nagoya_kagome.hours_raw: 7:30–13:30 (or until sold out); open Fri–Sun on the 2nd and 4th weekends of each month only. Morning eat-in set from 8:00.
nagoya_kagome.notes: [GF-dedicated] A fully wheat-free, dairy-free and egg-free rice-flour bakery — safe for celiacs since no wheat is handled on site (「小麦の取り扱いなし」). Everything from the shokupan loaves to bagels and focaccia is GF; nothing to avoid on the shelf. Note the very limited schedule: open only Fri–Sun on the 2nd and 4th weekends of the month, mornings only, and popular items sell out shortly after the 7:30 open, so go early and/or reserve via Instagram or text.

chef_bio.origin: 豊橋市, 愛知県 (Toyohashi, Aichi, Japan)
chef_bio.background: Kagome is a small husband-and-wife bakery in a residential corner of Sugiyama-cho, Toyohashi. The wife bakes the breads while the husband runs the shopfront and its small attached gallery, which hosts rotating art exhibitions. The bakery was built specifically around allergen-free baking — using no wheat, dairy or egg — to serve people with allergies and those seeking gluten-free food.
chef_bio.philosophy: To make gluten-free, allergen-friendly bread (no wheat/dairy/egg/refined white sugar) that is still genuinely delicious — famous locally for a 'surprisingly mochi-like' (驚くほどもっちり) rice-flour crumb — so that people with allergies can enjoy bakery bread safely.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour shokupan (米粉食パン) leavened with Shirakami-kodama yeast (白神こだま酵母), plus rice-flour bagels, focaccia and oatmeal breads.

anecdotes.text: The mochi-textured rice-flour bread is so popular it becomes scarce shortly after opening (オープン直後に品薄になってしまうほど人気).
A morning eat-in set from 8:00 pairs warm rice-flour bread with a drink, potage soup and a dessert.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト bakerykagome.net によれば「小麦・乳製品・卵（・白砂糖）を使用しないグルテンフリーのパン屋」で、白神こだま酵母を使った米粉食パンが中心、店内にギャラリー併設。号外NET 豊橋・田原の記事は夫婦経営で妻がパンを焼き夫が店を切り盛りする点と、もっちり食感の人気ぶりを伝える。グルテンフリーガイド（empacede）は小麦の取り扱いなしと評価。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 「グルテンフリー（小麦の取り扱いなし）」 — the shop handles no wheat on the premises, so there is no in-house wheat cross-contact source.
gf_cross_contamination.source_wording: 米粉パンの店 香米豆 Kagome ／愛知・豊橋 … グルテンフリー度 ★★★★★ ポイント 小麦、乳、卵不使用の米粉パンのお店です。 — and the list preamble: 「工房・店内に小麦粉を一切持ち込まず、すべての商品がグルテンフリーのお店は 90 店」「このページでは、グルテンフリーの米粉パン・お米パンだけを提供しているベーカリー 90 店 をリストアップしました。店内の商品はすべて小麦不使用・グルテンフリーです。」

gf_cross_contamination.text: 「当店の商品はすべて小麦・乳製品・卵不使用です」 — every product is made without wheat, dairy or egg.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Not applicable — bakery; no soy-sauce-based dishes served.

vegan_cross_contact.text: No dairy or egg is used anywhere in the facility, so vegan cross-contact from within the kitchen is effectively nil; sweeteners are plant-based (kibi/beet sugar, maple syrup).

staff_allergy_handling.text: The entire shop is purpose-built as an allergen-free (wheat/dairy/egg) bakery, so allergen avoidance is the default operating model rather than a special request.

positives.text: Rated ★★★★★ on the JP gluten-free guide with the note 「小麦の取り扱いなし」 (no wheat handled).
positives.source_wording: グルテンフリー度 ★★★★★ ポイント 小麦、乳、卵不使用の米粉パンのお店です。イートインスペースがあり、有料のコーヒーと、無料のレモン水があります。

positives.text: All products are simultaneously gluten-free, dairy-free and egg-free — fully suitable for celiac and vegan diners.

gf_review.why: Three separate attempts to disprove this one landed. First, the shop's own site claims only that its PRODUCTS use no wheat, dairy or egg (「当店の商品はすべて小麦・乳製品・卵不使用です」) — it never states the premises is wheat-free and never describes itself as a dedicated facility, so the own-claim half of the dedicated bar is not met at premises level. Second, the record cites the goguynet local-news article as corroborating evidence, but that article never mentions 小麦, gluten-free or allergens at all — it is a product review of the bread's texture, so the citation does not support what it is cited for. Third, the lineup includes 「オートミールを使ったちぎりパン」; uncertified oats in Japan are routinely cross-contaminated with wheat and barley during milling, which is a real celiac exposure route, and the record misframes this as an 'oat sensitivity' caution rather than a gluten-contamination one. That leaves jp.japan-glutenfree.com as the single genuine independent source, which the HARD RULE caps at options/ask.

Shop's own site makes a product-level claim only, never a premises-level wheat-free or dedicated-facility claim
Cited goguynet news article does not mention wheat, gluten-free or allergens anywhere — citation does not support the claim it is attached to
No cross-contamination statement published; the only caveat on the site concerns 白砂糖 in sourced ingredients
Only one genuine independent source (jp.japan-glutenfree.com); the cited empacede URL is dead and 301-redirects
Japan CAA warns 米粉 products frequently contain added wheat gluten or are made in wheat-handling rooms, with no mandatory contamination labelling
Open only 2nd and 4th weekends (Fri–Sun, 07:30–13:30) and sells out shortly after opening
gf_review.plain_rice: No — bakery, no plain gohan served.
gf_review.identity_note: The business is real and correctly described, but it is in 豊橋市杉山町 (Toyohashi), roughly 65 km and over an hour by train from Nagoya. The record files it under city 'nagoya' and calls Toyohashi 'Nagoya area', which is materially misleading for a city dining app. Reassign the city or scope it as an out-of-city day trip.

nagoya_solsol.gf_detail: A dedicated gluten-free rice-flour bakery with no wheat on the premises. The shop states 「小麦パンと厨房を分けるために、専門店として独立開業しました」(we opened independently as a specialty shop specifically to keep our kitchen separate from wheat bread) and 「小麦粉アレルギーがある方でも安心して召し上がっていただけます」(safe for those with wheat-flour allergies to eat with peace of mind). The Japanese celiac guide jp.japan-glutenfree.com rates it ★★★★★ and confirms 「全ての商品に小麦を使っていません」(none of the products use wheat). Because it is 100% wheat-free with a purpose-built separate kitchen, cross-contact risk is minimal, though seasoned buyers should still confirm any bought-in toppings.
nagoya_solsol.vegan_detail: Not a vegan bakery. Many items are dairy/egg-rich (cream bread, chocolate breads, custard, waffles), while some plain rice-flour loaves may be plant-based. No vegan labelling is published, so ask per item.
nagoya_solsol.hours_raw: Weekdays 11:00–17:00 / Weekends & holidays 11:00–18:00, closed Mon & Tue. May close early once the day's bread sells out.
nagoya_solsol.notes: [GF-dedicated] 100% wheat-free rice-flour bakery — the owner opened it as a standalone shop expressly to separate the kitchen from any wheat baking, so the whole product line is celiac-oriented. Its 花酵母のカンパーニュ (flower-yeast campagne) swept the 2024 2nd Delicious Rice Flour Bread Contest (Grand Prix + Gluten-Free Award). Go early: they bake a fixed batch and close when sold out. Closed Mon & Tue.

chef_bio.background: Katayama Yukihiro founded Bakeshop SolSol in Hekinan City after his nephew was diagnosed with a wheat allergy and could no longer eat ordinary wheat bread. Rather than baking gluten-free bread alongside wheat, he deliberately opened as a standalone gluten-free specialty shop so the kitchen would never share equipment or airborne flour with wheat products. Drawing on more than 15 years of bread-making, he works exclusively with rice flour (including Koshihikari) and his own SolSol rice-flour blends. In 2024 his 花酵母のカンパーニュ (flower-yeast campagne) took the Grand Prix, the Gluten-Free Award and the consumer-voted 'My Rice Flour Bread' award — a triple crown — at the 2nd Delicious Rice Flour Bread Contest in Yamagata.
chef_bio.philosophy: Make bread that people who cannot eat wheat can enjoy without compromise (小麦が食べられない人でも我慢せずに食べられるパン).
chef_bio.specialty: Flower-yeast rice-flour campagne (made with rare red-carnation flower yeast) and rice-flour breads/sweets, all wheat-free.

anecdotes.text: Opened as an independent specialty shop specifically to keep the kitchen separate from wheat bread; the origin was his nephew's wheat allergy.
花酵母のカンパーニュ won the Grand Prix (plus Gluten-Free Award and consumer 'My Rice Flour Bread' award) at the 2nd Delicious Rice Flour Bread Contest (2024), chosen from 111 entries as Japan's #1.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: solsol-gf.com (homepage, store, lineup) states it is a グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店 that separated its kitchen from wheat and that 花酵母のカンパーニュ won グランプリ at the 2nd contest; 中日新聞 (chunichi.co.jp) confirms the 全国3冠 (Grand Prix + Gluten-Free Award + My Rice Flour Bread) and that the origin was owner Katayama's nephew's wheat allergy; empacede rates it with no wheat handling.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Dedicated gluten-free premises — opened as a standalone shop expressly to keep the kitchen separate from wheat bread (「小麦パンと厨房を分けるために、専門店として独立開業しました」).
「全ての商品に小麦を使っていません」— none of the products use wheat (JP celiac guide, ★★★★★).

vegan_cross_contact.text: Not a vegan operation; dairy and egg are used in many items. No vegan cross-contact protocol published.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Founded around a family member's wheat allergy; the whole business model is wheat-free allergy safety (「小麦粉アレルギーがある方でも安心して召し上がっていただけます」).

owner_signoff.reason: Greg override of the proposed downgrade. The audit held it down partly because the shop frames its claim as 小麦アレルギー / グルテンフリー rather than セリアック. In Japan グルテンフリー is the ordinary term and セリアック is rarely used, so requiring that word eliminates good options without reducing risk. The own facility claim plus the national all-GF roster listing meet the bar.

gf_review.why: I went looking for a wheat line, a shared kitchen (the owner comes from a family of bread artisans, so a co-located wheat bakery was a live hypothesis), and any contamination complaint — and found none. The shop's own claim holds on its 商品へのこだわり page (「小麦グルテンを含む原材料は使用いたしません」, trading as a グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店), and independent celiac-grade corroboration is present: jp.japan-glutenfree.com lists it ★★★★★ on its national roster of bakeries where everything sold is gluten-free, noting 'all products contain no wheat'. Two further independent sources reinforce real GF handling: Chunichi Shimbun documents that owner 片山幸寛 built the business over 15 years to feed a nephew with a wheat allergy and that his 花酵母のカンパーニュ took the grand prize plus the グルテンフリー賞 at the 2nd 米粉パンコンテスト, and kodawarin.jp describes it as 「小麦を一切使わずに米粉パンを作るグルテンフリーパン専門店」 using 米粉100%. The one thing I could NOT verify is the record's headline quote about a separated kitchen — see red flags — but the dedicated bar is met without it.
red_flags: UNVERIFIED QUOTE: the record's 「小麦パンと厨房を分けるために、専門店として独立開業しました」 is attributed to solsol-gf.com/store/ but does not appear on that page and I could not find it anywhere — treat the 'purpose-built separate kitchen' detail as unsourced and strip or re-source it
Shop's own site publishes no cross-contamination protocol, allergen testing, or ppm threshold; the commitment page addresses ingredients only
Owner is from a bread-artisan family — confirm directly that no wheat baking occurs at or adjacent to the premises
Framing is 小麦アレルギー (wheat allergy) rather than celiac throughout; no celiac-specific review found
Cited empacede URL is dead and 301-redirects to jp.japan-glutenfree.com — sources need updating
Bought-in toppings and fillings are not ingredient-disclosed

Every item on the menu is made without wheat, so the whole product line is gluten-free; however no explicit celiac-grade cross-contact protocol (shared bowls/utensils) is published, so a strict celiac should confirm handling. nagoya_vegedeco_lab.vegan_detail: Several items are fully plant-based — the ヴィーガンチーズケーキ is egg- and dairy-free, and the salad cakes use tofu cream and 甘麹 sweetening rather than dairy or refined sugar. But not everything is vegan: the さつまいもタルト contains eggs and the honey (ハニー) soufflé variant uses honey. Ask per item.
nagoya_vegedeco_lab.notes: [GF] Fully wheat-free takeout studio — the entire salad-cake and sweets line is made with 大豆粉/米粉 instead of wheat flour, so celiacs can eat across the menu. Open only Fri–Sun 11:00–18:00, 5 min from Kawana subway station. No published dedicated-celiac cross-contact protocol, so confirm handling if highly sensitive; call 052-753-7775 to reserve cakes.

chef_bio.background: 森安美月 (Mitsuki Moriyasu) is a self-described Food Style Designer and representative of 株式会社Mitsuki Style, which created the VegedecoSalad® concept — non-sugar, gluten-free vegetable arrangements built to look like decoration cakes. The company also runs gluten-free menu consulting, and opened the Vegedeco Salad Lab takeout shop in Showa-ku, Nagoya (opened 15 July 2018). The concept originated from a French restaurant, La Porte Marseille, in Sakae (now closed).
chef_bio.philosophy: Food that makes both mind and body healthy — vegetables enjoyed beautifully, using genuine seasonings, functional ingredients, no refined sugar and no wheat.
chef_bio.specialty: ベジデコサラダ® (decoration-cake-style vegetable salads) and gluten-free, low-sugar sweets

anecdotes.text: Featured internationally: CNN 'FOOD SNAP JAPAN' (2017) reaching 200+ countries, and the BBC Travel Show (2018) named Vegedeco Salad Lab one of Nagoya's top three attractions alongside Nagoya Castle and the Science Museum.
Also covered by German TV 'Galileo' (2016), Hawaii's KHON2 Living808 (2018), plus Teen Vogue, Marie Claire and National Geographic Traveler.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト・食べログ・名古屋情報通によれば、株式会社Mitsuki Styleの森安美月が運営するグルテンフリー専門のテイクアウト店。小麦粉不使用で大豆粉・米粉を使い、CNN・BBC・独Galileo・ハワイKHON2など海外メディアに多数掲載。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Shop replaces wheat flour entirely with 大豆粉 (soy flour) and 米粉 (rice flour); the full product line is wheat-free, but no explicit celiac cross-contact protocol is published.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Sweets/salad-cake shop — soy sauce is not a primary ingredient; sweetening is via 甘麹 (fermented rice koji), not sugar or wheat-based seasoning.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Mixed line — some items use eggs (さつまいもタルト) and honey (soufflé), so vegan and non-vegan items are produced in the same kitchen.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No specific allergy-handling statement published; company does gluten-free menu consulting, suggesting allergen awareness. Confirm by phone (052-753-7775).

source_independence.note: This source reprints shop marketing rather than reporting a visit (a curated hub or a press release). It corroborates that a claim was MADE, not that it was verified.

positives.text: Entire menu is wheat-free using soy/rice flour; internationally recognised gluten-free specialist (CNN, BBC).
positives.why: The cited page is the company's OWN self-reported media list and says nothing about the menu being wheat-free. What it does show defeats the framing: BBC covered the shop as a Nagoya TOURIST stop alongside Nagoya Castle and the science museum, and the CNN piece is a travel 'salad cake' feature (cnn.

gf_review.why: Per the dressing brief I went after the dressings and the record's evidence base collapsed: the CNN/BBC recognition cited as a positive is the company's OWN media page, and both broadcasts covered the salad-cake visual novelty with no GF or allergen content, while the prtimes item is the company's own press release — so the independent count is effectively one local visit write-up (jouhou.nagoya). The GF framing here is 低糖質・ノンシュガー lifestyle marketing around a registered trademark, not celiac safety: no allergen statement, no cross-contact protocol, and the beet/koji/cocoa dressings and the marinated cabbage and carrot have NO published ingredient list, so wheat soy sauce in a dressing or marinade cannot be excluded. Damningly, the shop is absent from both Nagoya gluten-free guides I checked, including one compiled by a blogger with severe wheat allergy who cannot tolerate trace amounts.
red_flags: SOURCE INFLATION: internationally recognised gluten-free specialist (CNN, BBC) is sourced to the company's own media page; the BBC 2018 and CNN 2017 segments were tourism/visual-novelty features with no GF or allergen content
prtimes.jp entry is the company's own press release, not independent corroboration
Dressings (ビーツドレッシング, 糀ドレッシング, ココアドレッシング) and the marinated cabbage/carrot have no published ingredients — wheat soy sauce in a dressing or marinade is not excluded
GF is positioned as a 低糖質/ノンシュガー health-trend trademark (ベジデコサラダ®), not as celiac accommodation; no allergen or cross-contact statement anywhere
Absent from both independent Nagoya gluten-free guides checked, including one by a severe wheat-allergy blogger who vets shops for trace exposure
Only 1 Tabelog review; retail open Fri/Sat/Sun 11:00-18:00 only — very low third-party footprint to audit against
Not all items uniform: the sweet potato tart is reported to contain egg, so a blanket every-item-is-the-same claim is false
gf_review.identity_note: Business identity confirmed (株式会社Mitsuki Style takeout shop, 昭和区花見通1-96, near 川名 station, opened July 2018, still listed as open) — but note it is primarily a cooking-class studio; the retail counter runs only Fri-Sun and the shop's own /lab/ page presents the address as a classroom, so a visitor may find no retail service.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 1 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

existence.note: Ceased retail food service in October 2019 (own announcement 2019-09-23) and operates as a cooking-class studio. The cited website and menu_url are a class booking page.

chef_bio.background: Owner-representative 野口亜希子 founded the parent business VegeBio (ベジビーオ) as a healthy cooking studio on 2014-07-01, near Kurokawa station in Nagoya's Kita-ku. The name VegeBio combines 'Vegetable' and 'Biology,' reflecting her philosophy of building energetic, healthy daily life through vegetables and fruit. In 2017 the business expanded into retail and online sales, and after repeated customer requests to buy the cakes and baked goods from her classes, she opened the Ve Tree storefront (2022-01-11) as a dedicated vegan & gluten-free cake shop. The name 'Ve Tree' joins 'Ve' (vegan) with 'Tree,' symbolizing buds forming and blossoms appearing — growth.
chef_bio.philosophy: That truly delicious food should also satisfy the body's needs and be sustainable; sweets are positioned as 'reward treats' (ご褒美) that enrich life and serve as an entry point for customers to reconsider their broader eating habits.
chef_bio.specialty: Vegan & gluten-free cakes and baked sweets made with rice flour and soy flour, free of dairy, egg, wheat and white sugar.

anecdotes.text: The storefront was opened specifically in response to customers of her cooking classes asking to buy the cakes and baked goods themselves.
Media-noted as a rarity in Nagoya: a sweets shop where every single item is both vegan and gluten-free.
